classification.difficultyReason: Adds two oscillating graphical ordinates with different frequencies and no numerical x-scale.

spec.sourceRegion: Top of right column, question 52 continuation
spec.description: Unlabelled red one-cycle curve starts and ends at height 1; blue two-cycle curve starts at the origin, initially falls and ends on the x-axis. Only y=±1 is marked.
spec.mathematics: A normalized phase parameter reconstructs the visible one-cycle/two-cycle alignment. Internal drawing coordinates do not assert a numerical x-scale or supply equations for the source curves. No assignment of f or g to a colour is added.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied curves only; no sum curve.

answer.short:
The sum starts and finishes at height $1$. Between them it has a small trough, a small positive peak, a deeper negative trough and a higher positive peak, as shown.

Add the two ordinates at each common $x$; neither coloured curve needs to be identified individually as $f$ or $g$.
answer.worked:
At the y-axis, the supplied ordinates are $1$ and $0$, so the sum starts at $1$. Add the two signed ordinates along each vertical line. Where they cancel, the sum crosses the x-axis; where they have the same sign, the magnitude increases.

Plot enough ordinate sums to preserve the small first trough and peak, followed by the deeper negative trough and higher positive peak. At the right endpoint, the ordinates again sum to $1$. Join the plotted points smoothly.
